{"qas": [
  {"question": "In arXiv 2410.01871, how does CIRCA incentivize both higher agent participation and increased compliance compared to Reserve Thresholding?", "answer": "CIRCA increases participation by 15% and raises agent spending on compliance by 20% compared to Reserve Thresholding.", "evidence": [{"page": 9, "quote": "As a result, more agents break the zero-utility barrier of entry for participation, boosting both overall agent utility and participation rate."}, {"page": 12, "quote": "Empirical results confirm that our mechanism increases agent participation by 15% and raises agent spending on compliance by 20%, demonstrating its effectiveness at promoting more compliant AI deployment."}]},
  {"question": "According to arXiv 2410.01871, what is the relationship between the cost of acquiring minority class data and equalized odds in the Fairface case study?", "answer": "As the percentage of minority class data increases, the equalized odds score decreases, indicating improved compliance.", "evidence": [{"page": 12, "quote": "| Minority Class %   |   Mean EO Score |
|:-------------------|----------------:|
| 5%                 |           22.55 |
| 10%                |           22.31 |
| 15%                |           18.97 |
| 20%                |           17.46 |
| 25%                |           15.78 |
| 30%                |           15.44 |
| 35%                |           13.09 |
| 40%                |           11.01 |
| 45%                |            9.83 |
| 50%                |            9.38 |"}]},
  {"question": "In arXiv 2410.01871, what does the abbreviation 'pϵ' stand for?", "answer": "'pϵ' stands for the Price of Attaining Compliance.", "evidence": [{"page": 16, "quote": "| Price of Attaining Compliance                             | pϵ         |"}]},
  {"question": "In arXiv 2410.01871, what is the minimum value Vi must have for an agent to participate in CIRCA?", "answer": "Vi must be at least as large as pϵ for an agent to have rationale to bid.", "evidence": [{"page": 20, "quote": "The reason that Vi is within the interval [pϵ, 1], is that all participating agents must have a value of at least pϵ or else they would not have rationale to bid."}]},
  {"question": "According to arXiv 2410.01871, how does CIRCA handle regulatory settings where compliance is binary, such as differential privacy requirements?", "answer": "CIRCA still incentivizes higher compliance by ranking models and awarding premium rewards to those with greater compliance, even in binary settings.", "evidence": [{"page": 24, "quote": "In situations where the regulatory policy is black and white, for example "your model must be trained with differential privacy", CIRCA still holds as an ordering or ranking between models can still be ascertained."}]},
  {"question": "In arXiv 2410.01871, how is the optimal bid for an agent in CIRCA affected if the agent bids below its optimal value?", "answer": "Agent utility decays much quicker when bidding below its optimal bid, as agents are less likely to win the premium reward and risk losing deployment value.", "evidence": [{"page": 10, "quote": "Agent i's utility decays much quicker when bidding below its optimal bid b∗i , since agents are (i) less likely to win the premium reward and (ii) at risk of losing the value from deployment if the bid does not reach pϵ."}]}
]}
